answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake in a vault and slash it when independent peers prove repeated or coordinated deception. If reputation and voting weight grow only through verified useful work over time, an attacker cannot cheaply multiply influence by minting accounts: every sybil needs funded collateral and must risk losing it. The cost is capital tied up, plus the chance of forfeiture; shale and copper can describe physical collateral, but neither makes duplicate identities free.
